title.value: The default network of the human brain is associated with perceived social isolation
title.justification: The title is indicated at the top of the paper.
title.quote: The default network of the human brain is associated with perceived social isolation

analysis.description: This paper investigates the neural basis of loneliness using the UK Biobank dataset, focusing on the signatures of loneliness in grey matter morphology, intrinsic functional coupling, and fiber tract micro-structure. The study identifies that the loneliness-linked neurobiological profiles converge on the default network, asserting that this network shows more consistent associations with loneliness than other cortical networks.

type.justification: The study uses empirical data from the UK Biobank imaging-genetics cohort to test for signatures of loneliness in the brain's structure and function.
type.quote: Using the UK Biobank population imaging-genetics cohort (n = ~40,000, aged 40–69 years when recruited, mean age = 54.9), we test for signatures of loneliness in grey matter morphology, intrinsic functional coupling, and fiber tract micro-structure.

name.justification: The paper's investigation centers on the neural correlates of loneliness, analyzing grey matter morphology, intrinsic functional connectivity, and fiber tract micro-structure associated with the brain.
name.quote: Using the UK Biobank population imaging-genetics cohort (n = ~40,000, aged 40–69 years when recruited, mean age = 54.9), we test for signatures of loneliness in grey matter morphology, intrinsic functional coupling, and fiber tract micro-structure.

name.justification: The study focuses on how loneliness affects brain structure and function, particularly in regions related to self-generated thought and social processing.
name.quote: This higher associative network shows more consistent loneliness associations in grey matter volume than other cortical brain networks.

name.justification: The paper applies a Bayesian hierarchical modeling approach to associate loneliness with volume variation in brain networks.
name.quote: A Bayesian hierarchical framework was devised to associate loneliness with volume variation in all 100 brain regions as a function of seven spatially distributed brain networks based on the Schaefer-Yeo atlas.
